subject: Dedicated capacity add-on: tranche recommendation and contract addendum
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha@finlytics.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity planning ahead of renewal — Q1 utilization attached

Hi Rishi,

We’re coming up on our Dedicated contract renewal and the Q1 usage looks like we’re outgrowing the current pool faster than expected. I attached our internal utilization export (summarized below). Can you outline options and rough cost delta for adding capacity ahead of renewal vs. rolling the extra capacity into the next term? We’d like a recommendation we can present to procurement by next week.

Summary from our ops dashboard (April monthly averages):
- Sustained GPU utilization: 68-74%
- Peak utilization (daily batch windows): 92-96% for ~45–90 minutes
- 99th percentile latency-sensitive requests: small increase but within SLA so far
- Forecasted growth: +35% token volume over next 3 months (model usage + new embed heavy routes)

Key asks:
1) Recommended number/type of GPUs to add (A100 80GB equivalents preferred)
2) Time-to-delivery and impact on current SLOs during resize
3) High-level pricing (one-time add vs. committed tranche)

Procurement timeline: we need a paper-ready option by 2026-05-10.

Thanks,
Samantha Green
CTO, FinLytics
Samantha Green

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Samantha Green <samantha@finlytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning ahead of renewal — Q1 utilization attached

Hi Samantha,

I dug through the utilization CSV and ran it against the current job mix and latency profile you shared. Short summary + two pragmatic options below. I’ve attached a brief proposed_capacity_addendum_v1.pdf with the commercial placeholders.

Observed behavior (technical):
- Average sustained occupancy per GPU: ~71% (workload mix: 60% interactive chats, 30% embedding, 10% long-form batch jobs)
- Peak pressure windows: 45–90 minutes with near-saturation at 92–96% leading to queueing and modest latency spikes for interactive traffic
- KV-cache hit rates are high for chat routes (~82%), but embeddings produce the majority of token throughput growth

Recommendation A — Short-term tranche (fastest to provision):
- Add 6 x A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs (or 12 x 40GB-equivalent depending on vendor availability) as a dedicated tranche for 3 months, billed as an interim add-on.
- Expected immediate benefit: reduce average occupancy to ~45–55% and headroom for +35% growth, remove batch-induced peaks from interactive tiers.
- Pros: quick to deploy (2–5 business days), minimal contract changes (addendum), lower near-term cash commitment.
- Cons: higher effective $/GPU-month vs committed capacity.

Recommendation B — Committed term increase (preferred for unit economics):
- Increase committed pool by 8 x A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs for the next 12 months (roll into renewal).
- Expected immediate benefit: similar to tranche but with room for autoscaling/burst to cover unexpected peaks without queueing.
- Pros: ~20–25% lower unit price vs short-term add-on, bookkeeping aligned with renewal, eligible for a pricing credit for early commit.
- Cons: 7–10 business days for full provisioning and configuration if new hardware needs to be reserved.

Operational notes / migration impact:
- Live traffic will not be interrupted; we scale the dedicated pool and move model routing gradually. Expect a short window of increased scheduling as new hosts come up (~10–15 min of elevated trace activity).
- We’ll enable prefix/KV-cache warming before routing heavy traffic.

Commercial estimate (high level):
- Short-term tranche (6 x A10080 equivalent): ~USD 64k–72k per month (market proxy rates; final quote in addendum).
- Committed increase (8 x A10080 equivalent, 12 months): ~USD 46k–55k per month (after commit discount). Exact numbers in attached PDF.

If you want us to prioritize procurement-friendly docs, I can:
1) Draft a short commercial addendum with the two options and placeholders you can drop into a PO.
2) Prepare a one-slide TCO comparison for your procurement team.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call to run through the numbers — available 2026-05-06 10–12 PT or 2026-05-07 14–16 PT.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_capacity_addendum_v1.pdf

From: Samantha Green <samantha@finlytics.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-07T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning ahead of renewal — Q1 utilization attached

Hi Rishi / Dev,

Thanks — that breakdown looks sensible and maps to what we were expecting. Procurement prefers the committed increase if we can get a clear discount and a clause for a short-term tranche to cover immediate peaks while the committed units are provisioned.

Request from our side:
- Please prepare a formal addendum with the committed option as the primary line item and the 3-month tranche as a fall-back.
- Add a small clause for a migration SLA window and a schedule for prefix-KV warm-up activities.

Procurement timeline: we’ll circulate paperwork internally 05-10 and need a signed addendum by 05-24 to hit our budgeting window.

Samantha Green
CTO, FinLytics
